title: Span to Location refactor for non-text artifacts
description:
## Why

`Span` (`crates/cofferdam-core/src/span_util.rs`) is byte-offset based and assumes text-source artifacts. Fine for TypeScript. For binary, generated, or upstream-referenced artifacts (compiled IaC plans, generated code, ranges in non-text formats, SQL statements identified by index rather than character offset), byte offsets are awkward or meaningless.

`Span` flows through `Issue`, `RelatedSpan`, suppression directives, baseline files, formatters (text/JSON/SARIF), `cofferdam advise` output, and the plugin SDK surface. Generalising **now** (while the system is TS-only and the call-sites are countable in the hundreds) is cheap; doing it after a second adapter ships forces multiple coordinated migrations across the engine, the formatters, the plugin SDK, and every consuming tool.

This is a forward-compat refactor — the v3 work that cd-T3 (adapter contract) needs in place before a non-TS adapter can ship a finding that survives suppression and baseline workflows.

## What

Introduce:

```rust
pub struct Location {
    pub uri: Uri,           // file://, package://, gen:// schemes
    pub range: LocationRange,
}

pub enum LocationRange {
    /// Byte offsets in the source. Current Span behaviour.
    Bytes { start: u32, end: u32 },
    /// 1-indexed line/column pairs. For sources where lines are stable
    /// but byte offsets are awkward (post-formatter content, generated).
    LineCol { start: (u32, u32), end: (u32, u32) },
    /// Adapter-defined opaque range. Adapter namespace + opaque ID.
    /// Example: SQL migrations identify statements by index.
    Custom { ns: SmolStr, id: SmolStr },
}
```

- Migrate every public-facing `Span` to `Location` (`Issue::location`, `RelatedSpan::location`, etc.). Internal byte-range types used by TS-flavour checks can stay as `Span`.
- Refactor formatters to render any `LocationRange` variant coherently:
  - **text**: humans see "file.ts:12:5" or "migration_042.sql[stmt 3]"
  - **JSON**: stable additive schema; `range` becomes a tagged union; existing `start_line`/`end_line` fields preserved for byte-based ranges via a compat shim.
  - **SARIF**: byte/line-col ranges map natively; custom ranges use `logicalLocations` plus a `properties` bag.
- Suppression directives gain a `LocationRange`-aware identity scheme (depends on `cd-T6` adapter identity).
- Plugin SDK (`@cofferdam/check-sdk`) surface updated to expose `Location`; existing plugins keep working via a compat shim that wraps their `Span` outputs in `Location::bytes(...)`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Location` and `LocationRange` types in `cofferdam-core`; round-trip serialisation tests.
- [ ] `Issue` carries `Location` (or `Location` is constructible from `Span` for backward compat at the call site); built-in checks emit `Location::bytes(...)` and continue to pass their existing fixtures.
- [ ] All formatters handle each `LocationRange` variant. Document the SARIF degradation path for non-byte ranges.
- [ ] Plugin SDK exposes `Location`; existing plugins compile without source changes.
- [ ] Suppression directives parse a `LocationRange`-aware target syntax; existing byte-range suppression comments unaffected.
- [ ] No regression on existing fixture suite or real-repo validation (`bestefforttools`, `gistreact`).

## Sequencing

Can land independently of cd-T3 (the type and the byte-range variant ship first); the LineCol and Custom variants only become exercised when a non-TS adapter ships. Coordination with `cd-T6` (adapter identity) is on the suppression-target syntax, not the type itself.
design:
## Decision pending — multi-day refactor, strategic timing call

This is bounded work with clear acceptance, but it's a 3-5 day refactor touching every consumer of `Span` (built-in checks, plugin SDK, formatters, suppression parser, baseline format). It needs your timing call before I commit, plus a checkpoint structure so it doesn't ship as one giant PR.

### The timing question

**Now**: the bead's argument — "generalising now (system is TS-only, call-sites countable in the hundreds) is cheap; doing it after a second adapter ships forces multiple coordinated migrations." Pays a forward-compat tax of 3-5 days against a hypothetical future cost.

**Later (defer until cd-T3 / first non-TS adapter is real)**: avoids speculative work; lets the second adapter's actual constraints inform the type (LineCol vs Custom variant tradeoffs). Pays a one-time coordination tax probably ~1-2 weeks when the adapter lands.

The cost asymmetry isn't 5× — the bead's "multiple coordinated migrations" framing oversells the deferred cost. We have one Span definition, all call sites in workspace, and the engine is the only consumer. A coordinated migration alongside the adapter would be one PR, not many.

**Recommendation: defer until cd-9hp.10 (adapter contract) is at concrete-design stage.** The Custom variant's shape (opaque adapter-supplied id, or structured (kind, parts)) is meaningfully informed by the first non-TS adapter. Shipping `LocationRange::Custom { ns: SmolStr, id: SmolStr }` blind, before we know what an IaC plan range or SQL statement index actually looks like, risks one of:

- Re-cutting the variant when the first real adapter doesn't fit (which is the "coordinated migration" we were trying to avoid).
- Adding workarounds that pollute the type for the design's first real user.

### If we do it now anyway — checkpoint plan

Break into 4 PRs:

1. **Type ships, no migration** (~1 day). `Location` + `LocationRange` in `cofferdam-core`. `From<Span> for Location`. Round-trip serialisation tests. Nothing else uses it.
2. **Issue + RelatedSpan migrate** (~1-2 days). Add `location: Location` to both; keep `span: Span` as a deprecated parallel field, derived from `location` when only one was set. Built-in checks emit via `Location::bytes(..)`. Existing fixtures unchanged.
3. **Formatters + suppression parser** (~1 day). Text/JSON/SARIF render every variant. JSON schema bumps via the cd-9hp.12 versioning policy. Suppression target syntax extended for non-byte ranges (gated by the adapter identity work in cd-T6 — only the byte path exercised today).
4. **Plugin SDK** (~half day). `@cofferdam/check-sdk` exports `Location`; existing plugins continue to compile via a compat shim wrapping `Span` outputs.

Each PR ships behind no flag (the type is purely additive until step 2 makes `Issue::location` load-bearing).

### What I need from you

Pick one of:
- **A. Defer** (recommended). Close this bead with status=deferred until cd-9hp.10 has a concrete adapter target. I'll move on.
- **B. Do now, checkpoint #1 only.** I ship the `Location` type + tests as a no-op forward-compat landing; defer 2-4 until you're ready.
- **C. Do now, ride it through.** I sequence through all 4 PRs, asking only on schema-changing surface (JSON schema bump in PR 3).

Without your call I'm leaving this open and moving to the next bead.
notes: Deferred per design brief. Pre-emptive Span→Location refactor without a real second adapter risks designing the wrong Custom variant; coordinated migration alongside cd-9hp.10 is cheaper than the bead's framing. Reopen when cd-9hp.10 is in-progress and the first non-TS adapter's range semantics are concrete.

title: Adapter contract: source artifacts to canonical graph
description:
## Why

For cofferdam to support more than TypeScript, the ingestion layer (parser → corpus) must be a stable extension point. Today the pipeline is hardcoded: oxc parses, `crates/cofferdam-engine/src/graph.rs` extracts imports/exports, the rest of the engine runs against the resulting corpus. There is no contract a non-TS adapter could plug into.

The literature is consistent on what the right separation looks like: the **adapter** takes source artifacts and produces graph facts under a declared schema; the **consumer** (rules, `cofferdam advise`, formatters) operates only on the graph. Adapters cannot see rules or emit findings; rules cannot reach into source-language ASTs. Keeping these contracts disjoint is what makes a system support multiple source languages cleanly. See `docs/design-principles.md` §4 and the architectural review PDF §6 for the layered model.

The shared-rule test: when `"no public-internet exposure from a prod-* module"` can be written as one rule that applies to both Terraform and Pulumi, the contract is real. When it must be written as `terraform_no_public_ip` and `pulumi_no_public_ip`, cofferdam is a plugin system, not a generic engine.

## What

- Define the **adapter trait** (Rust) and an external-process / JS plugin variant: input is a project tree, output is graph facts emitted to the canonical schema (depends on `cd-T1`).
- Adapter declares:
  - The file globs it claims (`*.ts`, `*.sql`, `*.tf`, etc.).
  - The schema-extension namespace it emits under (`ts`, `sql`, `iac`).
  - Any taxonomy it registers (depends on `cd-9hp.3` configurable taxonomy).
  - Its identity scheme for findings (depends on `cd-T6` adapter identity).
- **Adapters are first-class**, registered in `cofferdam.toml` under `[adapters]` similarly to `[plugins]`.
- **Forbidden surface**: adapters cannot emit `Issue`s, cannot read rule configuration outside their declared inputs, cannot call user code. The contract is one-way: source → facts. Engine refuses to load an adapter that violates this.
- **The existing TS pipeline is refactored to fit the adapter contract** — it becomes the first adapter, not a special case. This is the proof that the contract is genuinely generic.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Adapter contract documented in `docs/adapter-contract.md` (input, output, allowed APIs, forbidden APIs, schema-extension rules, identity-scheme registration).
- [ ] TS pipeline refactored to implement the adapter trait; behaviour unchanged on existing fixture suite (`tests/spec-contract/` from `cd-9hp.8` is the validation harness).
- [ ] Engine refuses to load an adapter that tries to emit `Issue`s or read rule configuration; tested with a deliberate-violation fixture.
- [ ] **One non-TS adapter shipped end-to-end as proof-of-life.** Recommendation: SQL migrations (small initial schema, large potential audience, naturally distinct graph shape). Acceptance for that adapter is a sub-bead under this one once the contract is stable.
- [ ] Adapter SDK guide written for plugin authors: how to write a new adapter, what schema extensions are allowed, how to test.

## Sequencing

Depends on: `cd-T1` (canonical graph schema), `cd-9hp.3` (configurable taxonomy), `cd-T6` (adapter identity), `cd-T5` (Location refactor — adapters need non-byte-offset ranges). Tier 3 work; ships after the substrate is in place.

title: Corpus errors: namespace by check ID and add fallible API
description:
## Why

`CorpusIndex::with_slot` panics when two `CorpusKey<T>` constants share a name with mismatched `T` (`crates/cofferdam-core/src/corpus.rs:120-128`). Acceptable for compile-time-reviewed built-ins — a code review catches the collision. Hostile to plugins, where two unrelated authors might pick the same `"export.fingerprints"` name and crash the run.

## What

Two changes:

1. **Namespace slot names by owning check ID.** Engine prefixes the user-supplied slot name with the check's `meta().id` automatically, unless the check explicitly opts out (for genuine cross-check sharing). Eliminates the most common collision.
2. **Add a fallible API.** `try_with_slot(...) -> Result<R, CorpusError>` — returns `Err(TypeMismatch { existing, requested })` instead of panicking. Built-ins keep `with_slot` (panic on logic error), plugins use `try_with_slot`.

Document the collision rules in `docs/plugin-sdk-guide.md`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `try_with_slot` lands; existing `with_slot` callers unchanged.
- [ ] Slot-name auto-prefixing in plugin path; explicit shared keys still work for cross-check builtin sharing.
- [ ] Test demonstrating two plugins with the same naive slot name no longer collide.
- [ ] Plugin SDK guide covers the model.

Probably needs to land before cd-plugin-corpus to make that work safe.
close_reason: try_with_slot + try_with_namespaced_slot landed on CorpusIndex; built-in with_slot unchanged (delegates to try_with_slot for the type check, panics on the error path); CorpusError joined the cofferdam_core public surface; 4 new unit tests cover the collision matrix; docs/plugin-sdk-guide.md documents the contract. Plugin wire-up itself lands with cd-9hp.6 — this bead is the runtime.

title: Plugin corpus access for cross-file plugin checks
description:
## Why

Built-in Rust checks share state across files via `CorpusKey<T>` (`crates/cofferdam-core/src/corpus.rs:24`) — typed, key-addressed, per-slot mutex. The `@cofferdam/check-sdk` JS plugin runtime is per-file today (verify in `docs/plugin-sdk-guide.md`). For plugins to enforce *architectural* rules (cross-file: orphan exports, duplicate names, layered import audits) they need a corpus-equivalent.

## What

Design a corpus surface for plugins that respects Rust-side typing:

- **Option A:** plugin-namespaced typed slots — plugin declares slot schemas (JSON Schema?) at registration; cofferdam manages serialisation/deserialisation across the JS↔Rust boundary; collisions impossible because keys are auto-prefixed by plugin ID.
- **Option B:** opaque-blob slots — plugin gets `corpus.read(key)` / `corpus.write(key, value)` over JSON; collisions are the plugin's problem; simpler, fewer guarantees.
- **Option C:** restrict cross-file plugin checks to `finalize` callbacks that receive an aggregated context built by cofferdam (no slot writes, just reads).

Pick one. Worry about plugin-vs-plugin name collisions and plugin-vs-builtin collisions.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One example plugin that does cross-file aggregation (suggested: a duplicate-export-name detector).
- [ ] Plugin SDK guide explains the corpus story end-to-end.
- [ ] Tested against the plugin-sdk-e2e CI.

Depends on cd-corpus-namespacing landing first (see sibling bead).
close_reason: ctx.corpus.read/write/append + optional Check.finalize(ctx, opts) shipped on the SDK; plugin-host.mjs and Rust HostReport propagate corpus state and finalize findings (including the new related field) end-to-end; examples-plugins/duplicate-class is the cross-file fixture demonstrating the pattern; check-plugin-fixtures matches goldens for all 4 fixtures; SDK guide section rewritten with the full contract. Picked option B (opaque-blob, plugin-private namespacing) for v1.

title: observes_findings: expand with meta-checks or simplify by inlining
description:
## Why

`CheckMeta::observes_findings` (`crates/cofferdam-core/src/check.rs:100-108`) implements a deferred finalize phase that lets a check see the full pre-filter finding set. Today only `Consistency.UnusedSuppression` uses it. The mechanism is implemented, tested, and load-bearing for that one check — but otherwise undiscovered.

That makes it an extension point that's hard to find. We should either lean in (more meta-checks) or simplify (inline the suppression hook, drop the flag).

## What

Two paths:

**(a) Lean in** — seed 2–3 more meta-checks to validate the abstraction:
- `Refactor.RuleCofiring` — flag rules that always fire together (suggests consolidation).
- `Refactor.SuppressionNoise` — flag files where suppression density exceeds a threshold.
- `Design.RuleConflict` — detect cases where two checks disagree on the same span.

**(b) Simplify** — bake the suppression-staleness path directly into the engine; remove `observes_findings` from `CheckMeta`. Smaller surface, less to teach, but locks the engine to the suppression-only pattern.

A single ADR makes the call.

## Acceptance

- [ ] ADR records the chosen direction and why.
- [ ] If (a): at least one new observer check ships with fixture coverage.
- [ ] If (b): `observes_findings` removed; suppression-staleness logic inlined.
design:
## Decision: (b) simplify — inline the suppression-staleness path, remove `observes_findings`

### Why this not (a)

(a) leans in: ship 1+ observer checks to validate the abstraction.

The bead's three suggestions split cleanly into "needs cross-run state" (RuleCofiring) and "single-run feasible" (SuppressionNoise, RuleConflict). Even taking the easy ones, the cost is:

- Build the check + fixture + tests (~half day each)
- The new check has to earn its place against existing nudges (SuppressionNoise overlaps `Consistency.BroadSuppression`; RuleConflict's "disagreement" definition needs a non-trivial spec)
- "Validating the abstraction" by adding one synthetic user isn't validation — it's window dressing. Real validation would require organic demand, which six months have produced none of.

### Why (b)

The empirical signal is that `observes_findings` has had ONE user since it landed (`Consistency.UnusedSuppression`). The bead framing — "redeem the design pledges" — applies to extension points the design *promises* are extensible. `observes_findings` was never a documented surface; it's a single-purpose hook the engine grew to make UnusedSuppression work after cd-wqc. Inlining is the honest move.

What "simplify" means in code:
- Remove the `observes_findings` field from `CheckMeta` (workspace-internal; plugin SDK never surfaced it).
- The engine's two-phase finalize (Phase A: non-observers; rebuild ALL_PRE_FILTER_FINDINGS; Phase B: observers) collapses to: run finalize normally; UnusedSuppression's finalize body reads from a slot the engine populates with the post-non-finalize finding set, computed inline rather than via the observer hook.
- One special-case in the engine (UnusedSuppression-specific) vs. a generic mechanism with one user.

### What we lose

Plugins can't write observer-style checks. Today they can't anyway (plugin SDK doesn't expose the flag), so the loss is hypothetical.

### What we keep optionality on

If a second observer use case appears, re-extract: add the field back, restore the two-phase finalize. Reversal cost is a few hours; we have the git history to lift from.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `observes_findings` removed from `CheckMeta` and every call site updated.
- [ ] Engine's two-phase finalize collapsed; UnusedSuppression's input is computed inline.
- [ ] Existing suppression integration tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `docs/design-principles.md` reference to the observer pattern updated to reflect the simplification (or the ref removed if it was speculative).

Not done in this brief — work tracked under this same bead. Override with a follow-up `bd update --design` if you want (a) instead.

title: Configurable taxonomy: implement or remove the doc pledge
description:
## Why

`crates/cofferdam-core/src/check.rs:6` says the five-category taxonomy is *configurable* — projects can *add* categories, never remove the core five. But `Category` is a closed Rust enum at `check.rs:29`. Code does not match docs.

Either redeem the pledge (allow project-defined categories) or strike it from the doc.

## What

Two design options:

**(a) Open the enum** — `enum Category { Consistency, Design, Readability, Refactor, Warning, Custom(&'static str) }`. Plugin / config registers static names; `CheckMeta` stays `&'static`. Display order needs a deterministic policy for custom variants.

**(b) String-typed category with sentinels** — `category: &'static str`; engine validates against built-ins + a registered set. More flexible, less type-safe.

**(c) Strike the pledge** — close the enum semantics in the doc; ship without configurability.

Pick one, write a short ADR, ship.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/<n>-taxonomy.md` (or equivalent).
- [ ] Code matches docs.
- [ ] If we ship (a) or (b): one fixture demonstrating a project-registered category in `cofferdam.toml`; formatters group it correctly.
design:
## Decision: (c) strike the pledge

### Why (c) over (a) and (b)

**Reframe**: the architectural-review and cd-9hp.1's forward-compat addition pin the real cross-domain extensibility surface as **namespaces in check IDs** (`sql.foreign_key`, `iac.public_ip`, `gql.field`), not new top-level categories. The five-category taxonomy (Consistency, Design, Readability, Refactor, Warning) is orthogonal to the domain — a SQL forbid-pattern is `Design.sql.forbid_pattern`; a SQL line-length rule would be `Readability.sql.max_columns_per_row`. Categories describe *intent*, namespaces describe *domain*.

That makes "configurable categories" a vestigial pledge from before we worked out the namespace plan. The five categories are sufficient for every cross-domain check we can sketch today.

### Why not (a) — open the enum

`Custom(&'static str)` works at compile time but plugins can't supply `&'static str` for runtime-registered names. To make (a) actually plugin-reachable we'd need to widen `Category` to `String` / `Cow<'static, str>` everywhere — that's (b) in disguise, with extra steps.

Bare-engine projects could in principle declare custom categories in `cofferdam.toml` and have built-ins match them via string-equality, but no built-in check needs that today and no plugin example asks for it.

### Why not (b) — string-typed

Trades the type-safety the closed enum gives us (the formatter's category-grouping switch is exhaustive; cd-1c7 covers Other-bucket fallback for plugin ids with no dotted prefix). Buying optionality we don't yet need with safety we already have.

### What "strike the pledge" means in code

- `crates/cofferdam-core/src/check.rs:6` — remove the "configurable" claim from the module-level doc comment; replace with a one-line reference to the namespace plan (cd-9hp.1).
- Keep the closed enum exactly as-is.
- `docs/design-principles.md` — same doc-comment edit if it echoes the pledge.

### Optionality preserved

If domain adapters surface a real need for new categories (not new namespaces), reopen this bead and pick (a) or (b). The closed enum can widen later without breaking existing built-ins; widening is additive.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Doc comments at `check.rs:6` and (if applicable) `docs/design-principles.md` updated.
- [ ] Decision recorded inline above (this serves as the ADR; promote to `docs/decisions/` if/when the project adopts that directory).
- [ ] Closes cd-9hp.10's "configurable taxonomy" dependency — adapters use namespaces for their own check ids; categories stay as the existing five.

Bounded follow-up — I can ship this in a single edit after you sign off. Override with `bd update --design` if you want (a) or (b).
close_reason: Closed per design brief: the five-category taxonomy stays closed. Module doc + four design-principles.md spots updated to point at namespaced check IDs (cd-9hp.1 forward-compat) as the real cross-domain surface. Reopen if a future domain demands a new top-level intent bucket; widening is additive.

title: advise --diff: include plugin findings in would_fire / would_clear

title: doctor should warn when invariants.toml has empty [layers] (gh #17)
description:

description:
GitHub: https://github.com/TAJD/cofferdam/issues/12

`FileScope` (in `@cofferdam/check-sdk`) accepts:
```ts
export interface FileScope {
  readonly extensions?: readonly string[];
  readonly pathPattern?: string;            // singular
  readonly excludePatterns?: readonly string[];  // plural
}
```

A check scoping to several discrete file groups must use brace expansion in a single string. Works but harder to read than an array, and inconsistent with `excludePatterns`.

Approach: accept both forms.
- Add `pathPatterns: readonly string[]` (plural).

- Remove `pathPattern` in 0.3.0.

SDK is at 0.2.2 with low blast radius — could go straight to a breaking replacement, but accepting both costs ~5 lines and avoids forcing churn on early adopters.

title: cofferdam advise --diff <ref> — pre-flight validation for proposed changes
description:
Extension to 'cofferdam advise' (cd-lfx) that takes a working-tree diff (vs a git ref) and reports which rules WOULD fire if the change were committed. This is 'cofferdam check --since <ref>' (cd-3pn) flipped from after the fact to 'what would this change do.'

For agentic edit loops specifically, this collapses the feedback loop from 'write → check → fix → repeat' to 'advise --diff → done' in the cases where the agent's draft is rule-compliant on the first pass. Today the agent has to commit (or stage) and re-run check; this lets it preview the verdict on an in-memory or working-tree change without ceremony.

OUTPUT
Robot-mode JSON with two sections:
- would_fire: rules that would emit findings on the proposed change (the new violations the diff introduces)
- would_clear: rules that currently fire on baseline but stop firing in the proposed change (regressions cleared)

This dual surface matters for agents: an agent fixing one rule shouldn't break another silently. would_clear gives positive signal that work is on track.

ACCEPTANCE
- 'cofferdam advise --diff HEAD src/foo.ts' reports rules that would fire on the current working-tree version vs HEAD.
- 'cofferdam advise --diff main' (without a path) operates on the union of changed files in the working tree vs main.
- Output is robot-mode JSON with would_fire / would_clear sections.
- Works on staged diffs, uncommitted changes, and committed-on-branch diffs alike.
- Exit code: 0 when invocation succeeds, regardless of whether any rules would fire (the verdict is in the JSON, not the exit code) — agents need the JSON either way.
- A separate flag 'cofferdam advise --diff --fail-on=<level>' is allowed for CI use, mirroring the existing severity-gate ergonomics.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
- Reuses --since infrastructure (cd-3pn) for diff identification.
- For modified/added files: run the check pipeline against the post-diff source. If the file is in the working tree, that source is what's on disk; if --diff <ref>...<ref2> compares two committed states, materialize from git.
- For removed/modified files: re-run pre-diff checks to compute would_clear delta.
- Should reuse the engine's two-pass and corpus infrastructure — this is just running 'check' against an alternate source set.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Speculative advisory on uncommitted edits beyond the working tree. If we want to support 'agent has a candidate edit in-memory but not on disk yet,' file as a follow-up — likely needs a stdin-based source override.
- MCP wrapping. Lives in the cofferdam-mcp child bead.

DEPENDS ON
Parent: cd-hmb (epic).
- cd-lfx ('cofferdam advise <path>') — must land first; --diff is the diff-aware extension to it.
- cd-3pn ('--since <git-ref>') — CLOSED, supplies the diff machinery.

design:
# Implementation plan (drafted 2026-05-06, controller session)

## What it actually is

Despite living under `advise`, `--diff` is **not** an extension of the existing static-projection `advise <path>`. It runs the full check engine **twice** (against pre-diff and post-diff source) and diffs the issue sets. Closer architecturally to `check --since` than to `advise <path>`. The shared subcommand name is justified by the agent-UX framing: this is the call an agent makes *before* committing.

## I/O contract

```
cofferdam advise --diff <ref> [paths]
cofferdam advise --diff <ref> --fail-on=<level>
```

- `<ref>` = a single git ref. Pre-diff source is `git show <ref>:<path>`; post-diff source is the working tree (or `<path>`'s on-disk content).
- Output: robot-mode JSON (default to JSON since this is agent-targeted; text format optional).

```json
{
  "ref": "main",
  "would_fire":  [/* findings present in proposed but absent from baseline */],
  "would_clear": [/* findings present in baseline but absent from proposed */],
  "summary": { "would_fire": 3, "would_clear": 1 }
}
```

- Exit code `0` on successful invocation regardless of contents — verdict is in the JSON. `--fail-on=<level>` is the opt-in CI gate, gates on `would_fire` only.

## Issue identity for diffing — already solved

`crates/cofferdam-engine/src/baseline.rs` already keys findings by `(file, check_id, rule_signature)` where `rule_signature = sha256(trimmed_span_text)`. **Reuse this scheme verbatim.** Robust to line shifts and reformats (the proposed source has different line numbers from baseline; that's the whole point). No new identity infra needed.

## Only real new piece: file materialization at a ref

Today `cofferdam_engine::SourceFile { path, text }` is built from disk. Add to `crates/cofferdam-engine/src/since.rs`:

```rust
pub fn read_at_ref(repo_root: &Path, git_ref: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<String, SinceError>;
// shells out to: git show <ref>:<repo-relative path>
```

Edge cases:
- Added file (didn't exist at `<ref>`): `git show` returns non-zero → "no baseline source"; baseline issue set for that file is empty (everything in proposed becomes would_fire).
- Deleted file: `--diff-filter=AMR` already excludes deletions. Skip.
- Renamed: `--diff-filter=AMR` includes renames. v0 treats them as add+delete (accept the noise). Document the limitation.

## Engine plumbing

The check engine's analyse loop currently consumes `SourceFile` values built by `discover` reading from disk. Make sure the loop accepts `Vec<SourceFile>` directly so the diff path can construct them from `read_at_ref`. If the engine entry already takes `&[SourceFile]`, no change. Otherwise expose a thin `analyze_with_sources(sources: Vec<SourceFile>, ...) -> Vec<Issue>` API; the existing entry becomes `analyze_with_sources(discover(roots).map(read_to_source))`.

## Diffing

Standard set diff over `BTreeMap<(file, check_id, rule_signature), Issue>`:

- `baseline_set` = engine output on pre-diff sources
- `proposed_set` = engine output on post-diff sources
- `would_fire = proposed_set − baseline_set` (key-wise)
- `would_clear = baseline_set − proposed_set`

Carry the full Issue payload as the map value so the JSON output includes message + line/col + span.

## File-set scoping

Default scope = files changed in `<ref>...HEAD` ∪ working-tree changes vs `<ref>` (use existing `changed_files_since` plus an additional working-tree diff helper). Optional explicit `paths` arg restricts further. `--diff <ref>` with no paths and no changes ≡ empty result.

## Plugin checks

Plugins must run on both passes for the diff to be honest. Plugin host pipeline already accepts `(path, text)` input — drive it with materialized text rather than reading from disk. Performance: 2× plugin runs per file is acceptable; this command is not on the inner edit loop. Plugin metadata-only mode (used by static `advise`) is **not** sufficient here.

## CLI surface

In `crates/cofferdam-cli/src/main.rs` `Cmd::Advise`, add:

```rust
#[arg(long, value_name = "REF")]
diff: Option<String>,
#[arg(long, value_name = "LEVEL")]
fail_on: Option<Severity>,
```

Routing: when `diff.is_some()`, dispatch into a new `advise_diff::run` (separate module to keep `advise.rs` focused on static projection). Reuses config loading from `advise.rs`.

## File breakdown

| File | Action | Est. LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/cofferdam-engine/src/since.rs` | Add `read_at_ref` + `working_tree_changed_files` helper | +60 |
| `crates/cofferdam-engine/src/lib.rs` | Expose `analyze_with_sources` (or adapt existing entry) | ±20 |
| `crates/cofferdam-cli/src/advise_diff.rs` | New module: orchestrate pre/post runs, set-diff, JSON emit | +250 |
| `crates/cofferdam-cli/src/main.rs` | New flags on `Advise`, dispatch to `advise_diff::run` | +30 |
| `crates/cofferdam-cli/src/advise.rs` | Extract shared config-loading helper | ±10 |
| `crates/cofferdam-cli/tests/advise_diff.rs` | Integration tests with `tempfile` + `git` subprocess in fixture repo | +200 |
| `examples/advise_diff/*.ts` | Fixture: clean baseline + working-tree edit that adds a TripleEquals violation | +20 |
| docs (auto-regen via `gen_docs`) | `advise --diff` section | auto |

## Decisions before coding

1. **Two-ref form (`--diff a..b`)**: out of scope for v0. Single-ref only.
2. **Renames**: out of scope for v0; counted as add+delete.
3. **`paths` semantics with `--diff`**: when both are given, `paths` further restricts the scoped set.
4. **Performance**: full check run × 2. On bestefforttools-scale (325 files, ~270ms full check), expect ~600ms when most files changed; <100ms for typical small diffs (auto-narrowed file scope). No caching infra needed for v0.
5. **`--fail-on=<level>`** gates on `would_fire` only — `would_clear` should not block CI even at high severities (regression-cleared signal should never fail).

## Effort

~half a day end-to-end. Single-agent (controller) work — too much CLI/engine cross-cutting for a sonnet-builder one-shot, and the file-materialization API is a new public engine primitive that warrants design care. Use sonnet-builder for the integration-test fixture once the implementation skeleton is in place.

## Sequencing dependency

Lands after cd-5tz merges (cd-5tz touches `crates/cofferdam-cli/src/plugins.rs` which the diff-mode plugin runs share).

title: Suppression precedence: engine vs plugin magic-comments

- Plugin magic comments are parsed inside the plugin's run() function and prevent issues from being emitted in the first place.

Both must coexist. The BrandCasing e2e fixture (cd-7e4) exercises both deliberately. The rule needs to be explicit somewhere — SDK docs and a unit test in the engine.

title: Warning.UnusedImport — project-aware unused-import detection
description:
Project-level unused-import check that catches the cases tsconfig noUnusedLocals misses, specifically re-export passthroughs:

  // foo.ts
  export { Bar } from './bar';   // 'Bar' counted as 'used' by noUnusedLocals
                                 // but if no one imports Bar from foo.ts, this is dead.

By reading the project graph, we can confirm whether the re-exported symbol has any downstream consumer. If not, flag at the re-export site.

For non-re-export single-file cases (a plain unused import), defer to tsc/eslint — they already do it well at the file level. Cofferdam's value-add is the cross-file projection.

Configurable: project-aware mode (graph) vs file-only mode (defer to tsc).

EDGE CASES:
- Side-effect imports (// import './polyfill';) — never flag.
- Type-only re-exports — same logic, just type-aware.
- Default export re-naming chains.
notes: Child of cd-7h5. P3 — overlap with tsc/eslint means lower marginal value than OrphanExport.

title: Refactor.DeadExport — exported, imported, but never referenced
description:
Stricter than OrphanExport: exports that ARE imported but every consumer either marks the import as type-only-and-never-actually-uses-the-type, OR imports the symbol and never references it after import.

This is the post-refactor 'someone removed the use site but left the import + export' case. Quieter than OrphanExport (genuinely never imported) but more common in active codebases.

Requires the graph epic's per-file usage analysis: for each imported symbol, count references in the importing file's AST. Zero references = dead from that consumer; if all consumers are dead, the export itself is dead.

Lower priority than OrphanExport because false-positive risk is higher (e.g., dynamic imports via string keys, decorator-injected references).

title: [Onboarding] cofferdam doctor — diagnose install/config issues
description:
When a user's cofferdam install or configuration is broken, today they see a low-level error and have to figure it out themselves. 'cofferdam doctor' is the standard escape hatch for this class of problem (precedent: bd doctor, npm doctor, brew doctor). Critical when the install path crosses npm postinstall + prebuilt binary download + custom config — the failure surface is wide and the error messages are scattered.

Acceptance:
- New subcommand 'cofferdam doctor' (no required args). Runs a series of named checks and reports each as ✓ / ⚠ / ✗ with a one-line remediation hint on failure. Exit code 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail.
- Checks at minimum:
  1. Binary integrity: self-version matches expected, executable bit set (unix), runs without crashing
  2. Config: cofferdam.toml exists? If yes, parses cleanly? Unknown keys flagged as warnings.
  3. Baseline: .cofferdam/baseline.json exists? If yes, schema version matches? Findings reference still-existing files?
  4. Git: in a git repo (so --since works)? git binary on PATH?
  5. Discovery: at least one .ts/.tsx file under default scope, OR an explicit scope override in config?
  6. Suppression directives: any unknown check IDs referenced in source comments? (Re-uses the directive parser from cd-5t7.)
  7. (npm install only) bin/cofferdam(.exe) is the same version as the wrapper expects.
- '--robot' / JSON output: structured per-check result for consumers (the GitHub Action wraps doctor as a pre-flight).
- Documented in docs/getting-started/ and linked from any error message that doctor would have caught.

Design note: doctor is a diagnostic tool, not a fixer. It must NEVER auto-modify files (no auto-write of cofferdam.toml, no auto-rebaseline). Show the user what's wrong; let them decide. Fixers are 'cofferdam init' (config) and 'cofferdam baseline write' (baseline).

Standard for any npm package consumed in build pipelines.

Acceptance:
- 'CHANGELOG.md' at repo root following Keep-a-Changelog (https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) format. Headings: ## [Unreleased], ## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD, with subheadings Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security.

title: Refactor.CognitiveComplexity — mixed-operator rule (Sonar B3)
description: Today every &&/||/?? counts as +1. Sonar B3: a SEQUENCE of same-kind operators counts as +1 total; switching kind adds +1. So 'a && b && c' is +1 (one && sequence), but 'a && b || c' is +2 (one && segment + one || segment). Implementation: when entering a LogicalExpression that is itself the child of another LogicalExpression with the same operator, do NOT add — only the outermost (or kind-changing) one counts. Track parent-operator context via a stack. Fixture: a chain of && (score +1), a chain of || (+1), a mixed && and || (+2).

title: [A4] Suppression directives (// cofferdam-disable-...)
description:
Engine-level suppression directives, Biome-style primary syntax with ESLint-style aliases for refugees.

PRIMARY SYNTAX (Biome-inspired):
- // cofferdam-ignore: <CheckId>: <reason>            (next-line, default)
- // cofferdam-ignore-start: <CheckId>                (range start)
- // cofferdam-ignore-end                             (range end)
- // cofferdam-ignore-file: <CheckId>                 (file-wide, must be at top)
- ID-omitted form: // cofferdam-ignore                (suppress all on next line, engine emits info: 'broad suppression')

ALIASES (accepted, normalized to primary by formatter):
- // cofferdam-disable-next-line <CheckId>
- // cofferdam-disable-line <CheckId>
- // cofferdam-disable-block <CheckId> ... // cofferdam-enable-block
- // cofferdam-disable-file

REASON FIELD POLICY:
- Default off (optional).
- Required for Warning category by default.
- Per-check override via OptionSpec.

WHY BIOME OVER ESLINT:
Biome did the suppression design after a decade of watching ESLint accrete confusion (line vs next-line, block vs line comments, no reason field). One canonical form + a reason expectation produces less wallpaper-suppression. ESLint-style aliases honour muscle memory for refugees without bloating the canonical surface.

PARSING LOCATION:
Engine pre-pass (single comment-scan), not per-check. Engine maintains a suppression map and filters the final issue list. Keeps checks simple, makes interactions auditable.

INTERACTION WITH BASELINE:
Suppressed findings do NOT enter the baseline. (Cleaner than the alternative — a baselined-AND-suppressed finding is an audit trap.)

OUT OF SCOPE:
- IDE/LSP code-action to insert a suppression directive (separate bead).
- Linting the suppression directives themselves (e.g., 'unused suppression' check) — separate bead, classic third-pass work.

Unblocks cd-zaf (docs).

Suppression engine itself was already wired (Biome-style + ESLint aliases, 21 unit tests, plugin-issue path filtered in CLI), so the bead's remaining piece was the broad-form nudge. 6 new tests for the check. title: cofferdam-mcp — native MCP server for cofferdam tools
description:
Wrap cofferdam's most-useful subcommands as Model Context Protocol tools. An agent runtime that speaks MCP (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Continue, etc.) gets cofferdam as a first-class tool in its palette without needing to know the CLI exists.

DEPRIORITIZED TO P4: the CLI subcommands cover the core use cases first. MCP is a thin wrapping layer that adds value for users in MCP-enabled runtimes; better to ship the substrate (advise + invariants spec) and let MCP follow once the API shape is stable. Promote to P3 once cd-lfx and cd-9ph have landed and the API surface has stabilized.

WHY THIS COMPLETES THE EPIC
This is the cleanest answer to 'extend agent context' — the agent never carries cofferdam knowledge in its context window; it queries on demand. CLI shell-out works but couples the agent to a specific binary path and shell quoting. MCP gives the agent a structured tool with typed parameters and JSON responses, in the protocol agent runtimes already speak.

TOOLS TO EXPOSE
- cofferdam.check(path) — run checks on a path; returns findings as JSON
- cofferdam.advise(path) — JIT advisory (depends on cd-lfx)
- cofferdam.advise_diff(path, ref) — pre-flight validation (depends on cd-ugh)
- cofferdam.explain(rule_id) — rule rationale text
- cofferdam.invariants() — dump the project's invariants spec

ACCEPTANCE
- New crate 'cofferdam-mcp' (or 'cofferdam mcp' subcommand on the existing CLI) launches an MCP server over stdio.
- Five tools above are registered via the standard MCP tool schema and callable from Claude Desktop with a single config-file entry.
- Example claude_desktop_config.json snippet in docs/mcp.md gets cofferdam working in under 2 minutes for a fresh user.
- Example Cursor / Continue / Claude Code configs included where the runtime supports stdio MCP.
- Smoke test: round-trip a tool call from a test MCP client through the server and back.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
- New crate cofferdam-mcp depending on cofferdam-engine.
- Use an existing Rust MCP crate if one is mature enough; otherwise hand-roll the stdio JSON-RPC.
- Reuses the engine API directly — no new analysis logic, just a transport layer.
- Authentication: none initially (local-only stdio MCP; the server inherits the user's filesystem permissions).

OUT OF SCOPE
- HTTP/SSE MCP transport. stdio is sufficient for the local-tool use case; remote MCP is a separate trust model.
- Streaming responses for long-running checks. v0 returns the full result; streaming is a follow-up if check times warrant.
- Per-tool rate limiting, caching, or persistent state. The server is stateless — all state lives in the underlying engine and is recomputed per call.

DEPENDS ON
Parent: cd-hmb (epic).
- cd-lfx (advise) — for the cofferdam.advise tool
- cd-ugh (advise --diff) — for the cofferdam.advise_diff tool
- cd-9ph (invariants.toml) — for the cofferdam.invariants tool
- All can be implemented behind a feature flag if MCP work starts before all dependencies land; the cofferdam.check / cofferdam.explain tools can ship alone.

title: Dynamic VitePress sidebar from /docs/checks frontmatter
description:
In cd-cgw Phase 4 we hardcoded a static list of all 15 checks in docs/.vitepress/config.ts because import.meta.glob doesn't work in VitePress's config.ts loading context (Vite's loadConfigFromBundledFile uses plain Node ESM, not the Vite transform pipeline). Result: when a new check is added via cofferdam gen-docs, the docs/checks/<id>.md file is generated correctly but the sidebar doesn't auto-pick it up — must manually add an entry to config.ts.

Mitigations to investigate:
1. Have cofferdam gen-docs ALSO emit a generated TS file (e.g. docs/.vitepress/sidebar-checks.ts) with the static list, imported by config.ts. Sidebar still 'static' from VitePress's perspective but maintained by the same gen-docs run that produces the markdown. CI gate (gen-docs --check) catches drift. Probably the cleanest fix.
2. Use a pre-build script (Node.js) that reads docs/checks/*.md frontmatter and writes the sidebar list. Adds a tooling step.
3. Wait for VitePress to support import.meta.glob in config.ts (low-likelihood upstream change).

Recommend approach #1 — gen-docs already iterates all_builtins() and writes 5 artifact types, adding a 6th (sidebar-checks.ts) is mechanical.
close_reason: VitePress sidebar now generated by cofferdam gen-docs. New 6th artifact at docs/.vitepress/sidebar-checks.ts emits export const checksItems = [...] grouped by Category (Consistency/Design/Readability/Refactor/Warning), within each category sorted by id, with leaf text dropping the Category. prefix. config.ts imports from './sidebar-checks' instead of carrying the inline list. CI drift gate (gen-docs --check) covers it automatically — adding a new check via gen-docs updates the sidebar; if the committed sidebar-checks.ts diverges from what gen-docs would produce, CI fails. Verified: cargo clippy/fmt clean, 265 tests, gen-docs --check exits 0, pnpm docs:build succeeds (2.83s) with the expected 5-category structure.
